name: bpftop
desc: Dynamic real-time view of running eBPF programs
why: Live view of running eBPF programs is a rare window into kernel-level code execution happening on your machine.

brief.what_it_is: bpftop is a Linux command-line tool that shows eBPF programs currently loaded on the machine in a live, top-style table. For each program it lists the ID, type, and name, plus average runtime, events per second, and an estimated CPU percentage. It takes no input files; it reads kernel eBPF state and prints an interactive terminal UI. Pressing Enter on a program opens time-series graphs of its metrics, and it also shows which processes reference each program.
brief.why_it_exists: The README does not state a motivation in a single line. The project history notes it was formerly maintained by Netflix and is now an independent project maintained by Jose Fernandez, and the linked announcement is a Netflix tech blog post about streamlining eBPF performance optimization.
brief.how_it_works: bpftop uses the BPF_ENABLE_STATS BPF syscall command to turn on global eBPF runtime statistics, which are off by default to reduce overhead. It samples the statistics every second and computes average runtime, events per second, and estimated CPU utilization for each program in that window. When bpftop exits, it disables statistics gathering by closing the file descriptor that BPF_ENABLE_STATS returned.

commands_seen.context: Recommended install: the script downloads the latest release for x86_64 or aarch64, checks its SHA-256 against GitHub's published digest, and installs to ~/.local/bin (or /usr/local/bin when run as root). Accepts --version <tag> and --bin-dir <path>.

brief.install_notes: The install script is the primary path and covers x86_64 and aarch64 Linux. Distro packages exist for Fedora, Arch and Nix, and the README links to Repology for other packagers. Running requires sudo or root. The binary is dynamically linked to libz and libelf, so those must be present at runtime. Building from source needs zlib, libelf, clang and libbpf development packages (apt or dnf names are given), or the repo's Nix flake dev shell. Logging to the systemd journal is optional and falls back gracefully.
brief.standout: It turns on eBPF runtime statistics only while it is open and turns them off on exit, so the monitoring cost is paid only during observation. It also reports which processes reference each eBPF program, which is useful for seeing what is attached to the kernel.
brief.status: The README gives no release date or changelog, and I did not check the GitHub commit or release pages, so the status is unknown. It is packaged in Fedora, Arch and nixpkgs and has a published install script, which suggests active upkeep, but that is inference. The README says it moved from Netflix to independent maintenance by Jose Fernandez.
brief.caveats: Requires root (sudo) for all use, and the README says the tool will not run without it. Full functionality needs Linux kernel 5.8 or later; older kernels use a procfs fallback, with fewer details implied. Linux only. Shows nothing if no eBPF programs are loaded, so you need another tool such as bpftrace to generate some. Needs a terminal with ANSI colour and at least 80x24. The install script is fetched from bpftop.sh, which I did not open, so I cannot vouch for its contents. The README does not state a licence.
